description: Materialize the workflow workspace once at run start (verify-only on every dispatch) and harden the runner-owned bare repository cache against fetch-failure deletion and reference-unsafe replacement.

tasks.title: Harden the bare repository cache against fetch-failure deletion and reference-unsafe replacement
tasks.description: Rewrite WorkspaceManager.ensureCache() (packages/runner/src/runtime/workspace.ts) so a failed `git fetch origin` never deletes an existing bare cache. Limit cache replacement to an origin-URL mismatch or verified corruption (git fsck), and gate any replacement on an alternates-reference scan of the project's workspaces/ and landing/ directories so an object store still referenced by an active workspace is never deleted. Surface distinct outcomes: a cache-fetch failure is non-fatal on re-materialization (existing cache + workspace stay usable) but fatal on first materialization (no prior cache to fall back on); a blocked replacement is surfaced rather than silently skipped.
acceptanceCriteria: A transient `git fetch origin` failure on an existing cache leaves the cache directory in place, keeps a shared workspace's `.git/objects/info/alternates` valid, and does not delete or recreate the cache.
Cache replacement is refused (and surfaced) when any workspace clone under the project references the cache via `.git/objects/info/alternates`; the object store is preserved.
Cache replacement proceeds only when the cache origin URL no longer matches repository.gitUrl (or the cache is verified corrupt via git fsck) AND no active workspace references it.
On first materialization (no prior cache) a fetch failure is fatal; on re-materialization (cache exists) a fetch failure is non-fatal and the run keeps using the existing cache.
tasks.output: Hardened WorkspaceManager.ensureCache() with reference-gated replacement plus passing workspace.spec.ts coverage.
tasks.notes: Direct fix for the issue #180 cache self-corruption path (workspace.ts:212 delete-on-fetch-failure). Self-contained; no dependency on the materialize/verify split.

tasks.title: Materialize the workflow workspace once at the run start boundary; verify-only on every later dispatch
tasks.spec: specs/workspace-materialization/spec.md#Requirement: Workflow start materializes and binds the workflow workspace before the first task dispatch; specs/workspace-materialization/spec.md#Requirement: Work-item dispatch verifies the bound workspace without re-materializing it; specs/workspace-materialization/spec.md#Requirement: Workspace missing or corrupt is a workflow infrastructure failure; specs/workspace-materialization/spec.md#Requirement: mohist/prepare operates inside the bound workflow workspace; specs/workflow-run/spec.md#Requirement: REQ-WR-001 Starting an issue creates a WorkflowRun
tasks.description: Split WorkspaceManager.ensure() into materialize() (full clone/checkout/marker pipeline) and verify() (read-only marker + run-branch check), using the on-disk workspace marker (.mohist/workspace.json) as the once-per-run source of truth: marker present and matching issueId/issueNumber/workflowRunId -> verify-only; absent/mismatched -> materialize. Add a start-boundary precheck to WorkExecutor.execute() (packages/runner/src/runtime/executor.ts) that runs materialize-when-missing / verify-otherwise before any action executes, and remove the clone/checkout materialization from WorkExecutor.variables(). Keep the agent-job owner-kind on its existing standalone-workspace short-circuit (no materialize/verify). Emit distinct workspace-missing / workspace-corrupt / workspace-identity-mismatch failure kinds (reuse branch-invariant-violation for branch mismatches) as workflow-infrastructure failures attributed to the runner, not the task.
acceptanceCriteria: The first dispatch for a run materializes the workspace (cache prep, shared clone, base checkout, run-branch create/checkout, marker write); every subsequent dispatch in the same run calls only verify() and issues no remote `git clone`.
WorkExecutor.variables() no longer performs clone/checkout-style materialization while building variables for a work item.

A dispatch against a missing marker reports workspace-missing; a marker bound to a different run reports workspace-identity-mismatch; both are attributed to workflow infrastructure and neither is recovered by re-cloning.
An agent-job (owner-kind = agent-job) dispatch resolves its workspace from variables without invoking materialize() or verify().

mohist/prepare runs fetch+rebase against the already-materialized workspace without triggering materialization; prepare against a missing/unbound workspace fails as workspace-missing rather than materializing on demand.

Existing runner tests that assert 'server-supplied workspace.path still causes runner clone/materialization' (executor/workspace specs) are rewritten to assert the once-at-start contract, and a new cross-stage regression test proves an integrate-stage retry does not re-clone the workflow repository across plan->build->check->integrate.
tasks.output: WorkspaceManager materialize()/verify() split, WorkExecutor start-boundary precheck, distinct workspace-* failure kinds, and rewritten + new runner regression tests passing.
tasks.notes: Builds materialize() on top of the hardened ensureCache() from T-001 so the start boundary cannot re-introduce the cache-corruption path. The server already binds WorkflowRun.Workspace at start (IssueVariableBuilder/IssueGrain), so no server-side materialization state is added.

tasks.title: Surface workspace-materialization failures distinctly in CLI and web
tasks.spec: specs/workspace-materialization/spec.md#Requirement: Workspace missing or corrupt is a workflow infrastructure failure
tasks.description: Extend the failure-kind taxonomy in the CLI (packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/DeliveryFailureGuidance.cs and its TableRenderer consumer) and the web (packages/web/src/shared/lib/delivery-failure.ts) to recognize the workspace-missing / workspace-corrupt / workspace-identity-mismatch kinds emitted by the runner (T-002), with labels and next-action guidance that frame them as workflow-start workspace-materialization failures distinct from ordinary task failures (dirty-worktree / conflict / base-moved). The server already passes the structured task output through unchanged, so no server state or API change is required.
acceptanceCriteria: DeliveryFailureGuidance resolves the workspace-* kinds from structured runner output (and from message text where applicable) and renders a distinct label and next-action (e.g. 'Workflow workspace materialization failure') instead of a generic task failure.
Web delivery-failure.ts maps the same workspace-* kinds to a distinct failure-kind presentation, separate from conflict/base-moved/retry-safe/branch-invariant-violation.
A workspace-materialization failure renders differently from a dirty-worktree or ordinary task failure in both the CLI table surface and the web UI.

Tests cover kind extraction from output + message and the render paths (packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/Api/IssueCliTableRendererSpecs.cs delivery-failure matrix, and the web delivery-failure unit tests).
tasks.output: CLI and web failure-kind taxonomy extended for workspace-* kinds with passing extraction and render tests.
tasks.notes: Depends on T-002 having introduced the runner-side workspace-* failure kinds. No server-side change (structured output already passes through).
